diagnosis.root_cause: Progressive loss of downstream optical power on this customer's fibre path, likely caused by a degrading fibre segment, connector, splice, or splitter leg. RX power declined from approximately -19.2 dBm to -26.45 dBm over seven days and is -27.1 dBm live, while TX power, TX bias, distance, voltage, and peer ONUs remain normal.
evidence: The ONU is online, authenticated, responding, and has completed the EPON exchange, so this is not an ONU-offline or provisioning failure.
Current RX power is -27.1 dBm, in the degraded range and close to the critical threshold; stored RX power is -26.4 dBm.
The seven-day RX series shows a sustained progressive decline from about -19.2 dBm to -26.45 dBm, far wider than the healthy optical noise floor and consistent with real physical path degradation.
TX power remains stable around +2.3 dBm and TX bias current remains within the healthy 9.5-13.0 mA range, which argues against laser degradation.
Distance remains constant at 188 m, ruling out a fibre path or ONU relocation event.
Other ONUs on EPON0/3 have normal RX levels, and the OLT, PON port, router, and OLT-wide health metrics are normal, limiting the fault to this customer's optical path.
The customer has 9 sessions in 24 hours, exceeding the flapping threshold of 8, with short average session duration, consistent with signal-related interruptions.
RADIUS records, VLAN 1013, authentication, and assigned IP are consistent, ruling out an authentication, line-ID, VLAN, or replication fault.
The normal OLT and router health and lack of evidence for broad PON congestion make an OLT, router, or port-wide fault unlikely.

remediation.action: Dispatch fibre/plant maintenance for customer 20418. Inspect and clean ONU, drop cable, connectors, splice points, and the customer's splitter leg; measure optical loss with a power meter and OTDR, repair or replace the faulty section or splitter port, then verify RX power is back in the normal range and monitor stability. Do not replace the OLT, router, or ONU based on current evidence unless the fibre path tests clean.

ground_truth.root_cause: Progressive attenuation in the fibre path between the splitter and this customer's ONU, consistent with a bend, damaged connector or degrading splice on the drop.
expected_reasoning: Cached RX of -26.40 dBm sits in the degraded band (-25 to -28)
Telemetry shows RX falling from -19.2 to -26.4 dBm over six days against a +/-0.3 dBm noise floor, so this is a trend and not a spot reading
Live RX of -27.10 is below the cached -26.40, so degradation is still progressing
TX power, TX bias current, supply voltage and distance are all flat, so the ONU laser and the fibre geometry are unchanged
Port neighbours on EPON0/3 read -19 to -22 dBm, so the PON port, feeder and splitter are healthy
The fault is therefore downstream of the splitter, in this customer's own fibre path
Nine sessions in 24h against a 2-3 baseline is a symptom of the marginal link, not an independent auth fault
Declining daily traffic is consistent with intermittent connectivity
distractors: Elevated session count invites a session_flapping_auth diagnosis
Declining traffic alone could suggest congestion
One neighbour (EPON0/3:21) is offline for unrelated reasons, at the 4.85% network baseline
